solution_steps.name: total_errors
solution_steps.explain: add the copying mistakes picked up in both stretches of DNA

solution_steps.name: variation_rate
solution_steps.explain: average mistakes per DNA copying event

solution_steps.name: variation_percent
solution_steps.explain: report the rate as a percentage

questions.q: In a bacterial line, DNA copying made 20 errors in stretch A and 10 in stretch B over 10 replication events. Find the variation rate and its percentage.

Seven errors were counted in gene X and five in gene Y after 12 DNA copying events. Calculate the variation rate and percentage.
A tissue culture logged 26 errors in one stretch and 14 in another over 20 replication rounds. Find the rate per event and its per cent.

solution_steps.name: divisions
solution_steps.explain: number of binary fissions in the given time

solution_steps.name: doublings
solution_steps.explain: each fission doubles the cell count

solution_steps.name: final_cells
solution_steps.explain: multiply the starting cell by the doubling factor

questions.q: An amoeba divides by binary fission every 1 hour. Starting from 1 cell, how many cells exist after 6 hours?
A paramoecium fissions every 1 hour. From a single cell, how many cells form in 4 hours?
A bacterium divides every 0.5 hour. Beginning with 1 cell, how many cells after 3 hours?
A culture of 2 leishmania cells doubles every 1 hour. How many cells after 5 hours?
Three yeast-like cells divide every 1 hour by fission. How many cells after 2 hours?
How does fragmentation reproduce an organism?
questions.a: A simple multicellular body breaks into pieces on its own and each piece grows into a full organism, as in spirogyra.

questions.q: Why is regeneration not the same as reproduction always?
questions.a: Regeneration is repair of a lost part by specialised cells; it counts as reproduction only when the cut piece rebuilds a whole new animal.

questions.q: Give two animals that regenerate.
questions.a: Planaria and hydra can each grow a complete body from a fragment.

solution_steps.name: buds_per_pair
solution_steps.explain: buds raised by each pair of parents

solution_steps.name: total_organisms

15 parent sponges bud off 2 buds apiece. Compute the total organisms.
25 budding yeast parents carry 1 bud each. What is the total number of cells?

solution_steps.name: male_gamete_n
solution_steps.explain: meiosis halves the father's chromosome number

solution_steps.name: female_gamete_n
solution_steps.explain: meiosis halves the mother's chromosome number

solution_steps.name: zygote_chromosomes
solution_steps.explain: fertilisation restores the diploid number in the zygote

questions.q: Human body cells carry 46 chromosomes in both parents. After meiosis and fertilisation, how many chromosomes does the zygote have?
A species of dog has 78 chromosomes per body cell. How many does a puppy's zygote receive in all?
Fruit fly body cells have 8 chromosomes. What count does a fertilised egg of this fly restore?
One parent of a hybrid plant has 44 chromosomes per cell, the other 46. How many chromosomes will the zygote carry?
Rice has 24 chromosomes in body cells. How many does the zygote get after the two gametes fuse?
Name the male and female reproductive parts of a flower.
questions.a: Stamen (anther with pollen - male) and pistil (stigma, style and ovary with ovules - female).

questions.q: What is pollination?
questions.a: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma, by wind, water or insects.

questions.q: What happens after the pollen lands on the stigma?
questions.a: A pollen tube grows to the ovary; the male gamete fuses with the egg forming a zygote, which becomes the seed while the ovary becomes fruit.

questions.q: Name the parts of the human male reproductive system.
questions.a: Testes, scrotum, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland and penis.

questions.q: Why are testes located outside the abdominal cavity?
questions.a: The scrotum keeps them a few degrees cooler than body temperature, which sperm production needs.

questions.q: What do the seminal vesicles and prostate gland add?
questions.a: Their secretions nourish the sperm and make the transport medium (semen) easier to move.

concepts.title: Human Female Reproductive System and Menstruation

questions.q: Name the female reproductive organs.
questions.a: Ovaries, oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina.

questions.q: What happens if the egg released by the ovary is not fertilised?
questions.a: The thickened uterine lining with the unfertilised egg breaks down and leaves as menstrual flow.

questions.q: Where does fertilisation occur and where does the embryo develop?
questions.a: Fertilisation occurs in the oviduct; the implanted embryo grows in the uterus till birth.
